note: Imported by tools/import_headwear_green.py from a sheet whose person was painted flat #00FF00. The hat is simply everything that is neither the magenta backdrop nor the green person, so no head can leak into the frame and no colour heuristic can eat a hat pixel. The green silhouette also registers the cell against the mannequin on the WHOLE body rather than the torso alone. anchors are the hat bbox top-centre, crownNudge is anchor minus body-tops stand-<dir>-0, scale is 1. v2.3.2365: seated onto the eyes (southwest +4,-3px, east -8,+0px) -- every eyewear sheet so far has drawn the southwest cell low, and this moves each facing onto the eye row the game actually paints; bounded and reported by seat_eyes(). v2.3.2361: placed BY THE HEAD -- the vertical axis is calibrated on the drawn crown and cut line against the mannequin's, so a sheet returned at a different aspect still lands the piece where it was drawn on the face; the horizontal axis and the width come from the shoulder fit. Checked against the iris row the game paints (eyeMask.json). v2.3.2361: north omitted on purpose -- the eyewear is not visible from there. No png and no anchor for that facing, so the renderer hides the piece on it (the beard precedent, v2.3.1530). jog fitted by tools/tune_headwear.py --fit-pose jog: the jog sheets draw the head at a different size from the idle sheets, so scaleByPose carries headWidth(jog)/headWidth(stand) with the renderer's blanket poseTraitMul divided back out, and poseNudge scales the placement about the crown so the band does not slide down the face. mine fitted by tools/tune_headwear.py --fit-pose mine: the mine sheets draw the head at a different size from the idle sheets, so scaleByPose carries headWidth(mine)/headWidth(stand) with the renderer's blanket poseTraitMul divided back out, and poseNudge scales the placement about the crown so the band does not slide down the face. fish fitted by tools/tune_headwear.py --fit-pose fish: the fish sheets draw the head at a different size from the idle sheets, so scaleByPose carries headWidth(fish)/headWidth(stand) with the renderer's blanket poseTraitMul divided back out, and poseNudge scales the placement about the crown so the band does not slide down the face. hit fitted by tools/tune_headwear.py --fit-pose hit: the hit sheets draw the head at a different size from the idle sheets, so scaleByPose carries headWidth(hit)/headWidth(stand) with the renderer's blanket poseTraitMul divided back out, and poseNudge scales the placement about the crown so the band does not slide down the face. pickup fitted by tools/tune_headwear.py --fit-pose pickup: the pickup sheets draw the head at a different size from the idle sheets, so scaleByPose carries headWidth(pickup)/headWidth(stand) with the renderer's blanket poseTraitMul divided back out, and poseNudge scales the placement about the crown so the band does not slide down the face. v2.3.2380: south scaled to 0.912 (owner: "the south black glasses need to be shrunk a bit"). The number is fit-headwear-scale.mjs's own measurement for this facing (-8.8%, drawn width against a 43px head); only south takes it, because that pass measures width and a front view of glasses is the one facing where width is the right quantity -- the profile is one lens plus an arm, which is why the same pass asks east for +15% and must not get it. crownNudge.south y moves by bboxH*(s-s')/2 rather than the pass's full bboxH*(s-s'): holding the BOTTOM edge is correct for a hat on a skull and would drop these off the eye row, so the centre is held instead. v2.3.2390: the south temple arms are REMOVED (owner: "the current south idle black glasses view (I think thug life glasses) doesn't look correct the lenses look bent upward"). They were not bent: the lens rectangles measure dead level, top row 9 and bottom row 22 across both. What bent was the SILHOUETTE. The import turned the owner's long thin diagonal arm strokes into short fat wedges -- same taper (about 2% of the piece's width at the tip out to 12% at the hinge) but compressed into 9 rows instead of the 53 the sheet draws them over -- and a stubby triangle fused to the frame's outer top corner is not read as an arm going back over the ear, it is read as that corner lifting. Two raised corners over a level bridge is an upward bow, which is exactly what was reported. Every other pair in the catalogue draws this hinge as a 2-row stub above the frame (golden-glasses, goggles, 3d-glasses rows 0-1; white-glass 0-2); thug-life south had nine, and its own SOUTHWEST -- which was never complained about -- tapers from 2px. Clearing 256-space rows 6..14 leaves the frame's own end-caps, so the temple is still there; only the raised wing is gone. ANCHORS AND CROWNNUDGE ARE DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED even though the art's bbox top moved 6 -> 15: the anchor is a coordinate, not a measurement, so holding it renders every remaining pixel in exactly the place the owner already approved in v2.3.2380. Proven, not assumed -- a pixel diff of preview_headwear.py before and after changes only rows 99-113 of the south cell and nothing else in the sheet. bboxes.south is updated to the true content rect because it IS a measurement; nothing reads it for this item (hatHairFit only consults it for floatsAboveHair pieces, which this is not), so it stays honest for tooling without moving anything. scale.south stays 0.912: that number came from a WIDTH fit and the width is unchanged, the arms having lived inside the lens block's own column range.
